tasks.title: GA4 receives one-time auth tokens: the full URL of /reset-password and /verify-email links, token included
tasks.finding: GA4 is configured on every route in the root layout and sends the full page URL, query string included, as page_location (dl). Password-recovery links land on /reset-password?token_hash=…&type=recovery, and that page spends the token only when the form is submitted (rule 2.15), so a still-valid recovery token reaches Google Analytics on every reset visit. Anyone who can read the GA4 property's page_location before the token expires could use it to set the account's password. Email-change links (/verify-email?type=email_change&token_hash=…) send their token the same way, although that one is spent on load. Contentsquare, when NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_ANALYTICS is on, also records URLs. Found while verifying SEO-056.
evidence: Chromium via Playwright against next dev (2026-10-02), GA's /g/collect intercepted and stubbed: loading /reset-password?token_hash=PROBETOKEN0001&type=recovery produced a collect hit whose dl was that exact URL; loading /verify-email?type=email_change&token_hash=PROBETOKEN0002 did the same (the API it calls was stubbed so no real token was spent)
src/app/layout.tsx: gtag('config', 'G-D711W4RE25') with no page_location override, rendered for every route including (auth)
supabase/templates/recovery.html and rule 2.15: the recovery link carries token_hash to /reset-password, which makes no Supabase call until submit
tasks.recommendedChange: Owner, in GA4 now (no deploy needed): Admin → Data streams → the web stream → Redact data → turn on query-parameter redaction for token_hash, token, code and email. Then, as one reviewed change: stop sending auth query strings to analytics at all, either by setting a sanitised page_location in the gtag config (strip token_hash, token, code, type) or by not loading GA on the (auth) routes, with a test that fails if a token-bearing URL reaches gtag. Check Contentsquare's URL masking before NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_ANALYTICS is turned on.

Otherwise it runs the standard snippet: js, config G-D711W4RE25, and an async gtag.js. The check runs at document load, which is enough because every credential URL arrives by a full page load (email link, QR scan, pasted link) and none is reachable by in-app navigation; the JSDoc says the rule must move if that changes. Rule 2.23 records the invariant. Contentsquare is unchanged: it is off in production (NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_ANALYTICS=false) and needs URL masking checked before it is turned on.

tasks.title: Public pages still load the signed-in app's providers: Supabase client, react-query, service-worker registration, AuthRecovery
tasks.finding: Split from SEO-055. After the chart library left the public pages, they still load about 345 KB of gzipped JS. A chunk the audit measured at 245 KB raw (52 KB unused) carries the Supabase client, @tanstack/react-query, the service-worker registration and AuthRecovery, all mounted by the root layout for every route. They sit in the root on purpose: AuthRecovery is the hard-navigation escape for a broken session (rule 2.15), and the service worker's single-reload rule (2.19) assumes it runs on every full-document navigation. So moving them is an auth and PWA decision, not a bundle tweak.
evidence: src/app/layout.tsx mounts QueryProvider, ServiceWorkerRegistration and AuthRecovery around every route, the (marketing) group included
SEO-055's after-build: / still loads 344.9 KB gzip over 12 chunks with no recharts
tasks.recommendedChange: Measure first: which of these modules the public pages actually execute, and what each costs. Then decide with rules 2.15 and 2.19 in hand whether QueryProvider can move to the signed-in layouts, and whether AuthRecovery and the service-worker registration can load lazily on public routes. Lab scores are already 92–96, so this is a data and main-thread cost on mobile, not a ranking lever.
